circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Grand Prix location, following Bahrain and preceding later installations in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, is a street layout encircling Albert Park Lake that hosts the Australian Grand Prix and various other racing events annually. The track maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification, establishing it as a premier international motorsport venue.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally built as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, it was relaunched under a new name and resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan spanning 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km track that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and Australian V8 Supercars events, while holding FIA Grade 1 certification and offering multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish racing circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate over 140,000 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix continuously since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The venue's motorsport heritage extends back to 1925, and it was among the original locations on the inaugural Formula One calendar in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometer circuit serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its role as an F1 venue, the track has welcomed numerous international motorsport series, including World Sportscar Championship events, Champ Car competition, and various NASCAR categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the event returning from 2024 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone is a legendary racing venue that inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and later hosted the inaugural round of the Formula One World Championship in 1950. After sharing the British Grand Prix with other circuits between 1955 and 1986, Silverstone became its permanent home from 1987 onwards, while also hosting MotoGP racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986, marking a significant expansion of the championship's geographic reach during the Cold War era. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months near a major highway outside the capital, the 4. 381 km circuit became a permanent fixture on the F1 calendar, commemorating Hungarian motorsport heritage with its inaugural race dedicated to János Drapál, a pioneering local motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the 5. 793 km Autodromo Nazionale di Monza was constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue and the world's fourth such facility. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, save for a 1980 closure for renovation, making it one of only four circuits to appear continuously on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" through its characteristic long straights and swift corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsports venue situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, serves as a premier racing destination most notably hosting Formula One and Super Formula competition.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Strip along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout weaves past the region's most iconic destinations, including major casino resorts and entertainment venues like MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro, who died in separate racing incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Mexico's Formula One grand prix across three distinct eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" designation, following earlier hosting periods that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 corners and qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for Formula One, it joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the annual Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, closely following the harbour's edge in this tiny European principality. The track is officially known as Circuit de Monaco, though it is predominantly situated within Monte Carlo's district and is frequently called by that name.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that made a triumphant return to Formula One in 2021 after decades away, hosting the revived Dutch Grand Prix until 2026. The circuit earned its "Rollercoaster in the Dunes" nickname from its distinctive combination of steeply banked corners and dramatic elevation changes that wind through the seaside landscape, creating a uniquely demanding racing experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and measures 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was subsequently renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The venue hosts the Brazilian Grand Prix and features supporting facilities including a kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, serving as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021. The circuit also hosts international electric racing events from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout as a temporary street racing venue.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test of driver and car performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track accommodates major motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP, and World Endurance Championship races, while previously hosting various other racing series and championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career, along with 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, securing the 2018-19 world championship and multiple victories at prestigious events including Le Mans, making him the sole driver to excel across both Formula One and world sportscar competition at the highest level.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes for his Formula One debut in 2025 and has claimed eight victories in the championship since entering the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He competes at the highest level of motorsport competition.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 race victories. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while actively racing in European endurance competitions with Nielsen Racing. He has participated in seven Formula One events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver previously claimed victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver competing in Formula One with Red Bull Racing, representing France in international competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British racing driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, holding seven world championship titles that equal Michael Schumacher's record. He also leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently racing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved notable success in sports car racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One. He achieved runner-up status in the 2022 drivers' championship while with the Scuderia and has accumulated nine race victories throughout his career in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver whose Formula One career spanned 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the World Endurance Championship as a factory driver for BMW with WRT, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory during his time with Alpine represents a significant achievement in his career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending multiple seasons with Red Bull, where he finished second in the 2023 championship standings. Over his 15-year career in the sport, Pérez has accumulated six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One across 14 seasons from 2011 until 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his twelve seasons competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing in Formula One for Aston Martin, competing under his commonly used name rather than his full surname Strulovitch.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One world titles between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing, accumulating 73 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds a support position within the team's Formula One program.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced as Alpine since 2021, representing the sports car marque of French automaker Renault. Following Renault's factory team status from its earlier incarnation, Alpine competed in Formula One until Renault's withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One across multiple eras under different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited and racing under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, has been a constant presence in Formula One since the championship's inaugural 1950 season, making it the sport's longest-running team. With numerous championship victories and consistent competitiveness throughout its seven-decade history, the Scuderia represents the most successful organization in the sport's annals.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the outfit first competing in the 2016 championship season. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner, who departed in early 2024 after overseeing the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering company competed in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993, where it became one of the sport's longest-serving constructors. The team achieved notable success in sportscars, including overall victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours, before exiting F1 in 2025 as the fourth-oldest constructor by race starts. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundation for their own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership. The team competes under commercial sponsorship arrangements in the sport's premier championship.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, operates from Brackley under a German licence with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff as of January 2022. The marque's racing efforts are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" moniker.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor and team that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents the automotive conglomerate's second entry into the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull GmbH's second constructor entry on the grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from an English base, representing one of two F1 teams controlled by Red Bull GmbH since its establishment in 2005. Christian Horner led the team throughout its first two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's prior racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the championship as Atlassian Williams F1 Team from 2026 onwards.
